blocks.text: Source R says room B seats 12 and the meeting starts at 15:00. Generated answer says B seats 20, starts at 15:00 and includes free lunch.
Capacity 20 is contradicted; 15:00 is supported; free lunch is unsupported. One of three claims has support. The missing lunch fact is not evidence of no lunch.

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case
guided_practice.prompt: Source R says room B seats 12 and the meeting starts at 15:00. Generated answer says B seats 20, starts at 15:00 and includes free lunch. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Capacity 20 is contradicted; 15:00 is supported; free lunch is unsupported. One of three claims has support. The missing lunch fact is not evidence of no lunch.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Source S: trip is 18 km; vehicle speed is 6 km/h, constant, excluding stops. Answer says 2 hours, 18 km and includes lunch. Audit and recalculate.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Travel time is 18/6=3 hours under the stated assumption, so 2 hours is contradicted. Distance supported; lunch unsupported. Do not infer actual duration with unknown stops.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Source agreement and arithmetic validity are separate checks; missing evidence is not proof of the opposite claim.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
